title: Character: Quick Reads
summary: Discipline, ownership and the quiet work of becoming dependable.

cards.hook: Jocko Willink's blunt rule: there are no bad teams, only bad leaders.
cards.body: In *Extreme Ownership*, Willink and Babin describe SEAL task unit leaders who learned that when a team underperforms, the leader owns it. Not as blame, but as the only place a leader has power. A man who owns the outcome stops explaining and starts fixing. It works at home, too.

source.ref: Willink & Babin, *Extreme Ownership*, Ch. 2: No Bad Teams, Only Bad Leaders

cards.hook: Discipline isn't the opposite of freedom. It's where freedom comes from.
cards.body: Willink argues that the more disciplined your routines, the more freedom you buy. The man who trains regularly, keeps a budget and sets his schedule is free to spend money, take on challenges and say yes without chaos. Discipline now is the price of options later.

source.ref: Willink & Babin, *Extreme Ownership*, Ch. 12: Discipline Equals Freedom

cards.hook: Benjamin Franklin tried to become perfect, and wrote down every failure.
cards.body: In his autobiography Franklin lists thirteen virtues he wanted to build, including temperance, order, resolution and humility. He tracked them in a little book, working on one a week and marking each lapse. He never reached perfection, but he said the effort made him a better and happier man than he'd have been otherwise. The method, not the result, is what to borrow.

source.ref: Franklin, *Autobiography*, the project of moral perfection

cards.hook: Epictetus opens with a split that can end a lot of worry.
cards.body: Some things are up to us: our opinions, impulses, desires, aversions. Other things are not: our body, property, reputation, office. The Stoic move is to spend your energy only on the first group and meet the second with calm. It's a quick audit you can run on any worry: is this mine to control?

cards.hook: Take ownership of one thing you've been blaming on someone else.
cards.body: Pick one frustration at work or home where you've been explaining why it's not your fault. Ask: what part could I have done differently? Write one sentence, and take one action on it today. You're not accepting blame for everything, only claiming the part you can change.
